turns.assistant_text:
Here are some notable AI news highlights from today:

1. **Cisco Talos uncovers AI malware that ranks victims by dollar value** - A new AI malware has been discovered that assesses the financial worth of its victims. Bill Gates has raised alarms about rising AI cyber threats, warning that the world is not prepared for potential upheavals. [Read more](https://www.foxnews.com/tech/new-ai-malware-ranks-victims-how-much-theyre-worth) (Fox News).

2. **Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy** - Senator Ed Markey is questioning Google's policy that integrates AI features into K-12 student accounts, urging the company to allow schools to disable these features while still accessing Google Search. Critics argue that this policy could negatively impact students' mental health. [Read more](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ed-markey-google-ai-search-schools) (CBS News).

3. **AI hacking is getting worse — cyber firms are turning away victims** - Cybersecurity firms are overwhelmed by a surge in AI-fueled cyberattacks, leading some to turn away new clients seeking emergency assistance. The demand for cybersecurity services is skyrocketing as hackers increasingly automate their attacks. [Read more](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/security/ai-hacking-getting-worse-cyber-firms-are-turning-away-victims-rcna607617) (NBC News).

4. **First AI Casualties Looking More Like Roadkill** - An analysis discusses potential companies that may suffer as the AI bubble begins to deflate, highlighting CoreWeave, OpenAI, and Oracle as possible casualties. [Read more](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4965168-first-ai-casualties-looking-more-like-roadkill) (Seeking Alpha).

5. **Spy plot claims ensnare rock star CEO, a powerful Trump ally who pushed to bridge U.S.-China divide on AI** - Reports have emerged alleging that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted in a Chinese espionage operation, raising concerns about his relationships with U.S. and Chinese officials amid ongoing AI competition. [Read more](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/nvidia-jensen-huang-china-dismisses-spy-plot-allegations-ai-rcna608249) (NBC News).

These articles reflect the current landscape of AI developments and concerns.

items.title: Google faces mounting backlash for controversial AI school policy - CBS News
items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google's policy has drawn fire from other critics. In a statement posted on social media, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused the tech giant of "trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools."

Edited by Alain Sherter

An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services.
